data.name: Faalgun
data.gender_notes: Faalgun is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Faalgun is the name of the Hindu god of archery. He is also known as Shanmukha or Kartikeya and is the son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. Faalgun is considered the commander of the army of the gods and is worshipped for his courage, wisdom, and strength. The name Faalgun carries the meaning “God of Sharp Arrows” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Faalgun usually hope their child will grow to embody god of sharp arrows and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Faalgun belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Sharp Arrows.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Faalgun total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Faalgun is celebrated as a major festival in the Hindu calendar, in the month of Kartik, starting on the 11th day. It is also known as Kartik Purnima or Tripuri Purnima. During this festival, people take a holy dip in rivers, wear new clothes, offer prayers to Lord Kartikeya or Shanmukha. The festival involves various rituals, including listening to religious stories, donating to the needy, and singing devotional songs.
data.spiritual_significance: Faalgun is celebrated to seek the blessings of Lord Kartikeya or Shanmukha. He is considered the god of wisdom, courage, and knowledge. By worshipping him, people seek to purify their minds and souls. The festival also symbolizes the victory of good over evil. As the story goes, Lord Rama killed the demon king Tripura during this month, and the demon's three cities were believed to be destroyed. Therefore, the festival is also seen as a celebration of morality and good virtues over evil intentions.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Faalgun symbolizes the fierce, passionate, and transformative power of love. Associated with the Goddess of love, Kamadevata, this name invokes the intensity and creativity of love in all its forms. It encourages one to embrace the raw emotions of life and find joy in the journey.

historical_references.reference: The god Falgun is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata. He is depicted as the god of the red autumn leaf and the god of abundant harvests. He is also considered the god of the god of the fires of Agni, the god of the sky, and the god of the god of the wind.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Sanskrit epic that was likely composed between 400 BCE and 200 BCE.

historical_references.reference: Falgun is also known as the Hindu god of spring and is celebrated in the Hindu festival Holi. During Holi, people throw colored water and powders at each other in honor of Falgun, who signifies the victory of good over evil.
historical_references.context: Holi, also known as the Festival of Colors, is a widely celebrated Hindu festival that typically falls in late February or early March.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu name 'Faalgun' is predominantly associated with the Indian festival Holi, which is also known as the 'Festival of Colors'. This vibrant celebration takes place in late February or early March and involves people throwing colored powders and water at each other to mark the victory of good over evil. In addition to Holi, 'Faalgun' is also linked with the Punjabi harvest festival Lohri and the Hindu festival Diwali. On social media platforms such as Instagram, Twitter, and Pinterest, images and posts related to these festivals, including 'Faalgun', are popular all year round but particularly during the festive seasons. The use of hashtags like #Faalgun, #Holi, #Lohri, and #Diwali helps to spread awareness and engagement around these celebrations, showcasing traditional practices, modern adaptations, and inspirations for fashion, decor, and cuisine.
